identity.title: ALMA Spectral Imaging of Titan Contemporaneous with Cassini's Grand Finale

paper_type_evidence.quote: Whole-hemisphere, interferometric spectral maps of HCN, HNC, HC$_3$N, CH$_3$CN, C$_2$H$_3$CN, C$_2$H$_5$CN and C$_3$H$_8$ were obtained using ALMA in May 2017

evidence.quote: a mask diameter of $1.3''$ (8700 km at Titan’s distance of 9.26 AU)

question.value: What are the spatial distributions, abundances and chemical/dynamical lifetimes of Titan's nitriles and propane around the 2017 solstice, as seen by ALMA alongside Cassini CIRS?

evidence.quote: Here we demonstrate the use of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to continue Cassini’s legacy for chemical and climatological studies of Titan’s atmosphere.
as part of the director’s discretionary time program 2016.A.00014.S
Observations of Titan were carried out using the ALMA Band 7 receiver on 2017-05-08 and 2017-05-16

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two settings: 342-356 GHz and 349-364 GHz; spectral resolution 244-977 kHz (0.2-0.8 km/s)

evidence.quote: with 46 active antennas providing baselines in the range 15-1124 m
resulting in a spatial resolution of $\approx0.2''$ (using natural visibility weighting)
leading to RMS noise levels in the range 2-4 mJy beam$^{-1}$ MHz$^{-1}$

time_on_source.value: 18 min in setting 1, 138 min in setting 2

evidence.quote: The total on-source observing time was 18 min in setting 1 and 138 min in setting 2
as part of the director’s discretionary time program 2016.A.00014.S

provided.value: Nadir maps and limb spectra for HCN and HC3N (orbits #261, #275) for comparison with ALMA

evidence.quote: The data presented here were obtained on orbits #261 (2017-02-17) and #275 (2017-05-24)

what.value: Atmospheric density profile for the emission model

evidence.quote: The density profile was taken from (cite: kra09)

masking.value: 1.3'' diameter mask; threshold twice expected RMS

evidence.quote: a flux threshold of twice the expected RMS noise and a mask diameter of $1.3''$

continuum_subtraction.value: Low-order polynomial fits to line-free adjacent regions

evidence.quote: Titan’s continuum flux was subtracted using low-order polynomial fits to the (line-free) spectral regions adjacent to our lines of interest.

smoothing.value: Images degraded to circular PSF equal to the long axis of the beam for latitudinal profiles

evidence.quote: it was first necessary to degrade the resolution of our images so as to produce a circular PSF (with diameter equal to that of the long-axis of the original beam ellipse)
leading to a resolution of $0.15\times0.13''$ ($\approx900$ km) at 362 GHz

method.value: JAO pipeline calibration; days combined after regridding and Doppler-shifting to Titan's rest frame; position offset corrected; continuum subtracted; Clark clean

method.value: Spectra integrated in 4300 km radius aperture; features >3σ integrated into emission maps

evidence.quote: Spectral features greater than $3\sigma$ above the noise were identified and integrated to produce the emission maps

key_parameters.value: C2H3CN integration width 1.2 km/s per line, 360.8-361.7 GHz

evidence.quote: adopting a 1.2 km $\rm{s}^{-1}$ integration width for each spectral line

assumptions.value: Optically thin emission for most lines

evidence.quote: the majority of the observed molecular emission is expected to be optically thin
While the spatial resolution is significantly better than obtained by ALMA, the basic morphology of the resulting maps is similar, with a dominant south-polar emission peak for HC$_3$N

method.value: Average flux in radial wedges about Titan's center using circularized beam; east-west difference for HNC

evidence.quote: A wedge size $\phi_w=10^{\circ}$ was used for all molecules apart from C$_2$H$_3$CN and C$_3$H$_8$, for which $30^{\circ}$ was used
Use of a circularized beam renders this result free from any geometrical artifacts related to (elliptical) beam smearing.

method.value: Fit S(r) profiles with spherically symmetric model with polygonal abundance x(z), passed through ALMA simulator

evidence.quote: the resulting images were passed through the ALMA simulator (using the `Simobserve` and `Clean` tasks)
averaged within angular regions $\phi=45$-135$^{\circ}$ and $\phi=225$-315$^{\circ}$

assumptions.value: Optically thin emission; density from Krasnopolsky 2009; temperature from CIRS CH4 limb at -27 deg

evidence.quote: under the assumption of optically thin emission

fitting.value: Nonlinear least squares with MPFIT; 1σ errors from covariance matrix

evidence.quote: obtained through nonlinear least-squares optimization using the MPFIT routine (cite: mar12), and $1\sigma$ parameter errors were determined from the covariance matrix

validation.value: Contribution functions for altitude sensitivity; comparison with CIRS retrievals

evidence.quote: contribution functions (total flux as a function of altitude) were calculated within an ALMA beam centered at the respective $r_p$ value

analysis_steps.goal: Derive lifetimes from polar flux decay

method.value: Exponential decay of north polar flux from southern peak flux over 6 yr

evidence.quote: Assuming exponential decay of the form $dF_N/dt=F_Se^{-t/\tau}$, the following lifetimes $\tau$ were derived

assumptions.value: South pole at steady state; peak flux equals the north peak at 2011 reversal

evidence.quote: the peak of the spectrally integrated flux in the southern hemisphere ($F_S$) for a given species at the present epoch is taken to be representative of the peak flux that would have been present in the north

validation.value: Compared with Vuitton et al. 2019 model lifetimes

evidence.quote: These values are in reasonable agreement with the chemical/dynamical lifetimes ($L_{300}$) from the model of (cite: vui19)

analysis_steps.goal: Retrieve CIRS limb profiles for comparison

method.value: NEMESIS fit of -11 deg limb radiances from orbit #261

evidence.quote: The NEMESIS spectral inversion tool (cite: irw08) was used to fit the $-11^{\circ}$ limb observations from orbit #261
a cubic b-spline curve was fitted to the measured radiance profiles at each wavenumber using a knot spacing of 100 km
The profiles obtained are reliable for 180-400 km; below 180 km the line opacity was too high to allow an accurate determination, and above 400 km the signal-to-noise was too low.

findings_qualitative.value: HC3N, C2H3CN, C2H5CN show compact south polar peaks; HCN and CH3CN are more uniform in latitude

evidence.quote: whereas the HC$_3$N, C$_2$H$_3$CN and C$_2$H$_5$CN maps are dominated by polar emission, with the southern (winter) pole being strongest for the latter three species.

claims.hypothesis: HNC is confined to Titan's thermosphere and shows east-west asymmetry
claims.experiment: Limb profile modeling and wedge flux analysis of HNC map
claims.result: HNC above 730±60 km; E/W flux ratio 13±3%
claims.finding: HNC probes rapid ionospheric processes consistent with HCNH+ recombination model

evidence.quote: The HNC emission map shows an east-west hemispheric asymmetry of $(13\pm3)$%.

claims.hypothesis: ALMA and CIRS give consistent results for HCN and HC3N
claims.experiment: Compared maps and limb abundance retrievals
claims.result: Morphology and abundances in reasonable agreement
claims.finding: ALMA sub-mm results consistent with Cassini IR

evidence.quote: The ALMA sub-mm observations of HCN and HC$_3$N are consistent with Cassini infrared data on these species, obtained in the same month.

claims.experiment: Polar flux decay lifetimes compared with Vuitton et al. 2019
claims.result: Few-year lifetimes for C2H3CN and C2H5CN

evidence.quote: Chemical/dynamical lifetimes of a few years are inferred for C$_2$H$_3$CN and C$_2$H$_5$CN

why_this_data.value: Contemporaneous with Cassini's final flybys for complementary sub-mm and IR diagnostics

evidence.quote: the final opportunity for contemporaneous observations using ALMA and CIRS

evidence.quote: diurnal temperature variations seem an unlikely explanation for the observed HNC asymmetry
